reviews.name: Anything Everything
reviews.text:
In my experience, the summer camp at the Cary masjid was very disappointing. I enrolled my children hoping they would learn Islamic studies in a positive, supportive, and nurturing environment. Unfortunately, that was not what we experienced.

I felt that the children were treated too harshly, and one of the teachers came across as very rude, extremely strict, and lacking the patience needed to work with young kids. Instead of helping children improve, it often seemed like the staff struggled to manage the class and would place blame on the children when things didn't go well. That approach was upsetting to witness.

My concerns aren't based only on my family's experience. A relative also shared that their children had a similarly negative experience, which made me feel this wasn't an isolated incident.

The masjid itself is beautiful, and I appreciate the facility. However, based on my experience, I would not recommend enrolling children in its programs unless there are significant improvements in how the staff interact with and support kids. A positive learning environment should prioritize children's emotional well-being alongside their Islamic education.

I also personally felt that the way the programs were promoted gave more emphasis to enrollment than to the quality of the children's experience.

I sincerely hope this feedback is taken constructively so future families have a better experience.

reviews.name: Zeeshan Qurishi
reviews.text:
I am a Muslim male, and my fiancée is Catholic. We planned on having a Nikkah ceremony on September 22, at a nearby venue.

I first contacted this masjid in April and specifically explained our situation: I am Muslim, my fiancée is Catholic, she is not converting to Islam, and we wanted to have our Nikkah ceremony at a nearby wedding venue on September 22. I was told that this would not be a problem and that the masjid could perform the ceremony.

I called again in June and explained the exact same circumstances and date. Again, I was told there would be no problem.

I called again on September 15 to confirm everything. Once again, I explained that I am a Muslim male, my fiancée is Catholic and is not converting, and that the Nikkah was scheduled for September 22. I was again told that everything was fine.

On September 21 at approximately 9 PM, the night before our wedding, we received a call from the masjid telling us that they could not perform our Nikkah because my fiancée is Catholic. We were told that the only way they would perform the ceremony was if she converted to Islam.

The Masjid is entitled to have their own requirements. The issue is that we clearly explained our circumstances multiple times over the course of several months and were repeatedly told that there would be no problem. If the masjid could not perform the Nikkah under these circumstances, we should have been told in April, June, or at the very latest when I called to confirm on September 15, not at 9 PM the night before our wedding.

This created an enormous amount of unnecessary stress at an incredibly important moment in our lives. We had family traveling from Pakistan, Dubai, New Jersey, Guatemala, Alaska, Washington, Oregon, California, and other places to attend our wedding. Our ceremony had been planned around the information we were repeatedly given by the masjid.

My fiancée and I have also had serious conversations about our future family. We both agreed that if we have children, they will be raised Muslim. Nevertheless, the masjid waited until the night before our wedding to tell us that our Nikkah could not take place unless she converted.

After months of repeatedly being told that our Nikkah could take place, we were essentially put in a position where, the night before our wedding, we were told that the only way forward through this masjid was for my fiancée to convert. Whether or not that was their intention, that is an incredibly inappropriate last minute.

Thankfully, we are fortunate to know many Muslim families in the area. We were able to find another imam who agreed to perform our Nikkah at around 11 PM that same night, allowing us to have our ceremony the following day as planned.

This experience has seriously damaged the trust I, and our local muslim friends had in the masjid and its leadership. The Muslim friends we have in the area have also expressed that they no longer feel comfortable attending this masjid because of how this situation was handled.

This was supposed to be one of the happiest and most important times in our lives. Instead, the night before our wedding, we were forced to scramble to find an imam because a masjid that had been told our circumstances repeatedly for months suddenly decided it could not perform our Nikkah.

I have attached my call log showing that we did speak to the Masjid multiple times. I would not recommend.

reviews.name: MZ Rentals
reviews.text:
It is truly disappointing that I feel compelled to leave a review for an Islamic center, but I believe the community deserves transparency.

A masjid cannot be governed by friendships or personal loyalties. Those entrusted with serving on the board have a responsibility to remain impartial and make decisions based on justice, fairness, and the best interests of the community.

From my perspective, the decision to remove the imam appears to have been influenced by personal relationships rather than an objective process. That is deeply concerning. The imam is entrusted with providing religious guidance and leadership, and decisions affecting that role should never be driven by favoritism or internal alliances.

I believe the actions of Munawar Shah and Tanvir Iqbal have significantly undermined confidence in the board’s leadership. The community deserves a board that is unbiased, accountable, and committed to serving the masjid with integrity rather than personal interests.

My hope is that the leadership reflects on these concerns and takes meaningful steps to restore trust, transparency, and unity within the community.

The masjid had everything a woman needs. Small stove, bathroom, extra hijabs, even modest clothes for emergency, water, Quran. I was able to clean myself up and offer my salah on time. title: Masjid Ahlus Sunnah

ownerDescription:
Located in the heart of Reidsville, NC, the Islamic Center of Reidsville is a welcoming mosque and community space for prayer, education, and service. We hold the five daily prayers, Jummu’ah (Friday) prayer at 1:20 PM, and offer programs that support both spiritual growth and community connection.

Our masjid is open to anyone who wishes to learn more about Islam or join us in worship. In addition to religious services, we host educational classes, family events, and outreach programs to strengthen unity and provide benefit to the wider Reidsville community.

Whether you are a resident or just passing through, we welcome you to visit, pray, and connect with our growing community.
